issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for field 'numberOfInscribedStudents': the UML in problem_statement.md declares numberOfInscribedStudents as int, while the solution implementation declares it as long. This discrepancy will confuse students about the expected type and can lead to mismatches in constructor, getter/setter signatures and examples shown in the statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfInscribedStudents consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution field and its constructor/getter/setter from long to int to match the UML and problem statement, or update the UML/problem statement (and the template comments) to use long and adjust all related method signatures and documentation accordingly. Choose the option that preserves the intended numeric range for the exercise and update all references (UML, problem text, template, and solution) to the same type.

issues.description: Return-type / expression type inconsistency in getTotalNumberOfStudents(): the UML in problem_statement.md specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int and the solution declares the method as returning int, but the solution implementation computes the sum numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents where numberOfInscribedStudents is declared long in the solution. The expression therefore has type long and cannot be returned as int without an explicit narrowing conversion, causing a compilation error or hiding the underlying type mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the numeric-type inconsistency that causes the method to return an incompatible type. Either (A) change numberOfInscribedStudents to int in the solution (and update constructor/getter/setter) so the sum is an int and matches the UML, or (B) change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long (and update the UML/problem statement and any dependent methods) so the long sum is returned safely. Ensure all related methods (e.g., getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) and documentation are updated to use the chosen numeric type consistently.
